# topos-ffi

Bindings to the topos library for **TypeScript/JavaScript (WASM)**, **Python**, **Swift**, and
**Kotlin**, generated by [BoltFFI](https://boltffi.dev) 0.31 from [`src/lib.rs`](./src/lib.rs).

## API

Every language gets the same object and types:

| | |
|---|---|
| `Topos()` / `Topos.new()` | Default English book names and versification |
| `Topos.with_config(json)` | Custom `books`, `genres`, or `chapter_verses` (the same JSON as the CLI's `--data`) |
| `search(text, unit) -> [Match]` | Every reference in `text` |
| `parse(reference, style) -> Passage?` | One reference (`Jn 3:16` or OSIS `John.3.16`) |
| `complete(text, cursor, unit, style, limit) -> [Completion]` | Completions for the reference ending at `cursor` (`limit` 0 means no limit) |

- `Passage { book_id, book, reference, osis }`, written in the requested `BookStyle` (`Name`, `Abbreviation`, `Osis`)
- `Match { passage, start, end, line, column }`
- `Completion { label, kind, start, end, text }`: accept it by replacing `start..end` with `text`

**Offsets.** Languages index strings differently, so every offset (and column) is in the
`OffsetUnit` you pass, and `cursor` is read in that unit too:

| Language | Unit |
|---|---|
| JavaScript / TypeScript, Kotlin, Java | `Utf16` |
| Python | `Char` (code points) |
| Swift | `Utf16` (use `String.utf16` indices) |
| Rust, C, raw bytes | `Byte` |

## Building

Install the BoltFFI CLI once: `cargo install boltffi_cli --version 0.31.0`. Then run the pack
commands from this directory. Outputs go to `dist/` (gitignored).

| Target | Command | Needs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python | `boltffi pack python` | Python 3 | `dist/python/wheelhouse/*.whl` |
| TypeScript | `npm install && npm run pack:wasm` | `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`, Node | `dist/wasm/pkg` (an npm package named `topos`) |
| Swift | `boltffi pack apple` | macOS with Xcode | `dist/apple` (XCFramework and `Package.swift`) |
| Kotlin | `boltffi pack android` | Android NDK | `dist/android` (`jniLibs` and Kotlin sources) |

`npm install` here only installs what `boltffi pack wasm` needs to type-check the generated
code (`@boltffi/runtime`, `@types/node`, TypeScript); the script puts that `tsc` on the `PATH`.
Package names and the Kotlin package (`io.github.mastertemple.topos`) are set in
[`boltffi.toml`](./boltffi.toml).

## TypeScript / JavaScript

```sh
npm install ../path/to/topos/crates/topos-ffi/dist/wasm/pkg   # or publish dist/wasm/pkg
```

```ts
import { initialized, Topos, OffsetUnit, BookStyle } from "topos";

await initialized; // the WASM module loads asynchronously
const topos = Topos.new();

for (const m of topos.search("Read Jn 3:16-18", OffsetUnit.Utf16)) {
  console.log(m.passage.reference, m.passage.osis, m.start, m.end); // John 3:16-18 John.3.16-John.3.18 5 15
}

const input = "see Gen 1:";
const [first] = topos.complete(input, input.length, OffsetUnit.Utf16, BookStyle.Name, 10);
const accepted = input.slice(0, first.start) + first.text + input.slice(first.end); // "see Genesis 1:1"

topos.dispose(); // free the Rust object (or let the finalizer do it)
```

- The package picks the right loader for Node, browsers, and bundlers through its `exports`.
- `Topos.withConfig(json)` returns `null` for an invalid config in JavaScript (other languages
  throw an error with the reason).
- A runnable project is in [`examples/node`](./examples/node): `npm install && npm start`.

## Python

```sh
pip install dist/python/wheelhouse/*.whl
```

```python
from topos import BookStyle, OffsetUnit, Topos, ToposErrorException

topos = Topos()
for m in topos.search("Read Jn 3:16-18", OffsetUnit.CHAR):
    print(m.passage.reference, m.passage.osis, m.start, m.end)

passage = topos.parse("1 Cor 13:4-7", BookStyle.NAME)  # None if it is not a reference

try:
    custom = Topos.with_config(open("bible.json").read())
except ToposErrorException as error:
    print(error.error.message)
```

The wheel is built for the Python that ran `boltffi pack python`. A runnable script is in
[`examples/python`](./examples/python/example.py).

## Swift

Add `dist/apple` as a local Swift package (it contains `Package.swift`), then:

```swift
import Topos  // `module_name` in boltffi.toml

let topos = Topos()
for m in topos.search(text: "Read Jn 3:16-18", unit: .utf16) {
    print(m.passage.reference, m.start, m.end)
}
let custom = try Topos(withConfig: json)  // throws ToposError.invalidConfig(message:)
let completions = topos.complete(text: input, cursor: UInt32(input.utf16.count),
                                 unit: .utf16, style: .name, limit: 10)
```

## Kotlin

Add `dist/android/jniLibs` and the Kotlin sources in `dist/android/kotlin` to an Android module, then:

```kotlin
import io.github.mastertemple.topos.*

Topos().use { topos ->  // AutoCloseable
    for (m in topos.search("Read Jn 3:16-18", OffsetUnit.UTF16)) {
        println("${m.passage.reference} ${m.start}..${m.end}")
    }
    val completions = topos.complete(input, input.length.toUInt(), OffsetUnit.UTF16, BookStyle.NAME, 10u)
}
val custom = Topos(json)  // throws ToposError.InvalidConfig
```

The TypeScript and Python snippets are run as part of the examples above. The Swift and Kotlin
snippets come from the generated bindings but were not compiled here, since that needs Xcode or
the Android NDK.
